subject: issues with dates on x-axis in R graphics

messages.author: facd70bca72970b7
messages.subject: issues with dates on x-axis in R graphics
parts:
I'm studying diachronic change in Old French, specifically change in subject-verb order over the course of about three centuries. I have texts representing 16 different dates, starting in 980 and ending in in 1279. From the structure of my data frame, it's clear that R interprets this as a numeric variable, as intended, but when I plot it (either using plot or barplot), R appears to graph it on the x-axis as a categorical variable, with 16 equally spaced points (although in reality, they are far from equally spaced). I've tried specifying the limits of the x-axis manually, which just piles the points up right next to each other near the beginning of the x-axis. Since 980 is my 0-th date, I've also tried assigning the 16 points in time numbers from 0-299, representing the time period I'm investigating. This also has no effect on the graphing of this variable. I'd appreciate pointers as to how to deal with this. Thanks! 

Laurie Zaring

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Re: issues with dates on x-axis in R graphics
parts:
What you seem to be wanting to do, I would do like this (reproducible example!):

# generate data
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)); set.seed(1)
DATE <- rep(seq(1400, 1700, 25), each=15)
ORDER <- sample(letters[1:2], 195, replace=TRUE)

# generate proportion table and plot it
props.of.b <- prop.table(table(DATE, ORDER), 1)[,2]
plot(names(props.of.b), props.of.b, type="b", ylim=c(0, 1),
xlab="Date, all texts", ylab="rate of Germanic inversion with Sn"); grid()


And that works - why don't you try that?
